branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Fever and Cutaneous Lesions in a Patient with Multiple Myeloma

state.case_summary:
A man in his late 60s presented with a 10-day history of fever up to 38.5°C and tender lesions on the neck and trunk. Past medical history included a 10-year history of IgG-κ multiple myeloma, with recent first cycle of chemotherapy (ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone) in the previous month for disease recurrence.

Examination revealed annular erythematous plaques of up to 2 cm in diameter, with violaceous and crusted centers on the neck and trunk. On the right chest, there was an annular erythematous lesion with 2 zones of color—a central area of purpura and an outer erythematous and edematous ring.

- Laboratory findings:    - White blood cell count: 2.3 × 103/μL (reference: 3.5-9.8 × 103/μL)    - Hemoglobin: 12.1 g/dL (reference: 13.5-17.6 g/dL)     - Platelet count: 29 × 103/μL (reference: 130-400 × 103/μL)    - C-reactive protein: 3.31 mg/dL (reference: <0.30 mg/dL)    - Blood culture: negative  - Skin biopsy findings:    Image Title: Clinical image of annular erythematous plaques    Image Description: Annular erythematous plaques on the chest        Image Title: Histopathologic image    Image Description: Inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells in superficial and mid dermis        Image Title: Cellular detail image    Image Description: Infiltrated cells showing large, elongated, vesicular nuclei, single inconspicuous nucleoli, and scant, slightly eosinophilic cytoplasm        Image Title: Immunohistochemical image    Image Description: Myeloperoxidase-positive cells        Additional findings:    - Immunohistochemistry: Positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138    - Nuclear dust present without obvious leukocytoclastic vasculitis    - Mild papillary dermal edema

excluded_candidates: Infection: considered due to fever and low white blood cell count, but blood culture is negative
Leukocytoclastic vasculitis: considered due to purpura, but not obvious on histopathology
